Was Delivered Therein As Under:
Coram: Hon'Ble Dr. Justice Chillakur Sumalatha
 Oral Judgment

Heard Sri.R.Shashidhara, learned counsel for the appellant as well as Sri.S.Krishna Kishore, learned counsel for respondent No.3.
2.

Dissatisfied with the amount that is awarded as compensation, the injured is before this Court challenging NC: 2024:KHC:32512 the order that is rendered by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Jagalur in MVC No.373/2019 dated 20.03.2020.

As against the claim for Rs.24,50,000/-,
the Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.1,62,581/- as compensation.
With a contention that the amount awarded as compensation is too meager, the present appeal is filed.
3. Sri.R.Shashidhara, arguing the matter, submits that the appellant as an agriculturist was earning Rs.18,000/- p.m.
However, the Tribunal for the reasons best known took the notional income as Rs.9,000/- p.m. which is unjustifiable.
Learned counsel also states that the appellant sustained two grievous injuries and took extensive treatment.
Pw.2 deposed with regard to the treatment taken by the appellant and the aspect of disability.

Though sufficient material was produced to show that the disability is 30% which is permanent in nature, the Tribunal assessed and took the disability as 6%

2 which is improper.

sentences.text: Learned counsel also contends that NC: 2024:KHC:32512 the amount granted as compensation under all other heads is also low.

4. On the other hand, the submission that is made by the learned counsel Sri.S.Krishna Kishore,
learned counsel for respondent No.3 is that the injuries are healed and therefore, the Tribunal rightly assessed the disability in respect of whole body as 6% which needs no interference.
Learned counsel thereby seeks to pass necessary orders.
5. As per the material available on record, the appellant sustained fracture of left Zygomatic bone and hemorrahage contusion of right frontal lobe.
It is not in dispute that the appellant took treatment as inpatient at Yennapoya hospital, Mangalore, SSIMS hospital and also took treatment as outpatient at Chigateri hospital.

However, considering the totality of the evidence produced, this Court is not inclined to disturb the finding that is given by the Tribunal with regard to the assessment of permanent physical disability.
However, as NC: 2024:KHC:32512 rightly submitted by the learned counsel for the appellant, Sri.R.Shashidhara, the Tribunal did not assess the notional income of the deceased in a proper way.
Admittedly, the accident occurred in the year 2018.
The Karnataka State Legal Services Authority is taking the notional income as Rs.12,500/- p.m. for the relevant period.
Therefore, this Court considers desirable to adapt the said figure for the purpose of calculating the compensation.
The multiplier that is applicable is 16.
Thus the loss of future earnings due to permanent physical disability if calculated will be as under:
Notional monthly income Rs.12,500/-
Annual income Rs.1,50,000/-

On applying appropriate Rs.24,00,000/-
 multiplier 16 Loss of future earnings due to Rs.1,44,000/- permanent physical disability being 6%
6.
This Court is of the view that the amount of compensation granted under all other heads also requires enhancement.
Undisputedly, the appellant would have NC: 2024:KHC:32512 taken bed rest at least for a period of 2 months.

Thus loss of earnings due to laid up period comes to Rs.25,000/- (Rs.12,500X2).
7.

Thus, the compensation which the appellant is entitled to will be as under:

sentences.text:
In the light of the forgoing discussion, the following:
NC: 2024:KHC:32512 ORDER (i) Appeal is allowed in part.
(ii) The compensation that is awarded by Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Jagalur through orders in MVC No.373/2019 dated 20.03.2020 is enhanced from Rs.1,62,581/- to Rs.2,39,901/-.
(iii) The enhanced amount shall carry interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
(iv) Respondent No.3 is directed to deposit the enhanced sum within a period of 8(eight) weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this order.
(v) On such deposit, the appellant is permitted to withdraw the entire amount.

Sd/-
